finding.summary: Acceptance criteria claim content/export paths report code "ERROR" for an Express-shaped 404, but the code they describe (formatter.ts) throws `UpstreamHttpError` with `readonly code = 'HTTP_ERROR'`, which `outputError`'s `errorCode()` reads directly — so the content/export path also reports `HTTP_ERROR`, not `ERROR`. The doc's own file (`formatter.ts:132-135`) even states the intent is that both paths report the *same* `HTTP_ERROR` code so an agent needn't branch on which command it ran — directly contradicting the acceptance criterion two sections later.
finding.evidence: "An Express-shaped 404 body reaches stderr as `{\"error\":{\"code\":\"ERROR\",\"message\":\"HTTP 404\"}}` on the content/export paths" — checked against packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:137-138 (`class UpstreamHttpError { readonly code = 'HTTP_ERROR'; }`) and the docstring at formatter.ts:132-135 ("Carries `code` so `outputError` reports the same `HTTP_ERROR` that `upstreamErrorJson` writes"), and formatter.ts:41-46 (`errorCode` reads `error.code` when present). The content/export path (forwardUpstreamError -> throw UpstreamHttpError -> outputError) therefore yields `HTTP_ERROR`, not `ERROR`, for a non-envelope body.

verdict.reason: The reviewer's quoted "evidence" misstates the document. The actual acceptance criterion (docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:55-60) reads: "An Express-shaped 404 body reaches stderr as `{\"error\":{\"code\":\"HTTP_ERROR\",\"message\":\"HTTP 404: <upstream message>\"}}`, exit code 1 — the **same** code on every path (content/export as well as import/upload/download), because both describe the identical condition and an agent must not have to branch on which command it ran to know what the code will be." It says HTTP_ERROR, not ERROR — matching exactly what formatter.ts:132-138 implements (UpstreamHttpError with `code = 'HTTP_ERROR'`, whose docstring at formatter.ts:132-135 states the same intent). There is no contradiction between the two sections of the doc; the reviewer fabricated a mismatch by substituting "ERROR" for "HTTP_ERROR" in the quoted text.
